texts.text: Weather Report

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Another week of scattered extreme weather brought heavy rains to some regions. Thunderstorms early in the week brought large rain accumulations and strong winds to the western regions with Manitou seeing a maximum windspeed of 90 km/hr and Minitonas accumulating 37 mm of rain on August 31. Severe storms on September 6 and 7 brought strong winds and heavy rains to parts of the Central and Interlake regions. Portage la Prairie received 86.9 mm in just one hour on September 6. Other areas that saw intense hourly accumulations include Stonewall, Selkirk, Woodlands, and Elie. Powerful winds caused significant damage throughout the City of Winnipeg and west of Elie.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to September 7 range from 230 mm to 356 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Since May 1, large areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have accumulated more than 350 mm of precipitation. Seasonal accumulations are above normal for the majority of the Northwest and Southwest regions. Large areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have seen accumulations over 120% of normal. A few localized areas of the Interlake, Central and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 90% of the 30-year average.

texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There was a good start to the week, as most producers started harvesting and grain was dry by Saturday. Heavy rains on Sunday in the early afternoon put a stop to all harvesting, as most areas received rain, with some areas reporting hail. Several areas received over 2 inches of rain. There are now a lot of lodged crops, making harvest even more difficult than it already was. Cereal grain quality has already started to deteriorate, with some producers reporting sprouting. There is also severe lodging in most canola crops, primarily due to a mixture of disease, heavy rains, and strong winds.

texts.orig: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The region was very dry this past week; however, many locations received enough rainfall Sunday evening to benefit long-season crops, especially corn and soybeans.
texts.text: The region was very dry this past week; however, many locations received enough rainfall Sunday evening to benefit long-season crops, especially corn and soybeans.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overall, the dry conditions have allowed producers to make good progress with harvest. Cool nights and heavy dews have occasionally delayed harvest and resulted in much of the harvested crop requiring additional drying.
texts.text: Overall, the dry conditions have allowed producers to make good progress with harvest. Cool nights and heavy dews have occasionally delayed harvest and resulted in much of the harvested crop requiring additional drying.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye harvest is complete. Spring cereal harvest continues, with spring wheat yield and protein percentages ranging from average to good. Barley yields are reported as slightly above average. Oat test weights, however, are lower than typical, likely due to lower soil moisture during critical development stages.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye harvest is complete. Spring cereal harvest continues, with spring wheat yield and protein percentages ranging from average to good. Barley yields are reported as slightly above average. Oat test weights, however, are lower than typical, likely due to lower soil moisture during critical development stages.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans are at the R6 - R7 growth stages. The crop would still benefit from additional rainfall. In areas where soil moisture is lowest, leaves are already yellowing and dropping due to a combination of limited rainfall and hot temperatures. Many plants are producing predominantly two-seeded pods, with very few four-seeded pods. Pod abortion has also occurred in the upper canopy in many fields. The soybean crop is now past the stages where soybean aphid is a concern, and populations appear to be naturally declining, likely due to the abundance of beneficial insects in fields. White mold (Sclerotinia) is showing up in some soybean fields. This is primarily occurring in fields with the most crop growth, which are likely also among those with the highest yield potential.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Almost all of the pea crop has been harvested, with the remaining fields expected to be completed over the coming days. Quality has been good, while yields have been average.
texts.text: Almost all of the pea crop has been harvested, with the remaining fields expected to be completed over the coming days. Quality has been good, while yields have been average.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest and swathing continue. Late-season diseases, including sclerotinia and verticillium stripe, are noticeable. More canola is being swathed this year than in recent years, likely due to increasing levels of verticillium stripe. Pre-harvest sprouting has also been an issue in some fields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Corn ranges from the late milk to early dent stages. Although the crop would benefit from additional rainfall, the majority of the corn crop appears to have fared relatively well despite the dry conditions experienced over the past few weeks.
texts.text: Corn ranges from the late milk to early dent stages. Although the crop would benefit from additional rainfall, the majority of the corn crop appears to have fared relatively well despite the dry conditions experienced over the past few weeks.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Sunflowers are at the R7 to R8 growth stages.
texts.text: Sunflowers are at the R7 to R8 growth stages.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Many producers are mowing down patches of weeds, particularly kochia and amaranth species suspected of herbicide resistance. Producers are also taking advantage of soybean fields that are turning color to scout for potential waterhemp and Palmer amaranth plants, which can be more easily identified and rouged at this stage. Producers are also scouting recently harvested cereal, pea, and canola fields for new waterhemp emergence and regrowth. Amaranth species can emerge in late August and early September and may produce seed before freeze-up.
